title.en: Some, any; how much, how many
title.it: Some, any: un po', del; quanto
title.de: Some, any: etwas, ein paar; wie viel

rule.en:
**some** and **any** are for an amount you don't give exactly. They go with plurals (**some apples**) and with things you can't count (**some honey**, **some bread**).

**some** is for positive sentences: **We've got some eggs.** Also for offers and requests, where you expect yes: **Would you like some tea?** **Can I have some water, please?**

**any** is for negatives and most questions: **There isn't any bread.** **Have you got any honey?** **Are there any fish in the tarn?**

Countable nouns have a plural (a sheep, fifty sheep; an apple, apples). Uncountable ones have none and take no a: honey, bread, water, milk, hay, weather, news. Ask **how many** with countable ones and **how much** with uncountable ones: **How many sheep?** **How much honey?** **a lot of** goes with both: **a lot of sheep**, **a lot of honey**. In negatives and questions, **many** and **much** are common too: **We haven't got much time.**
rule.sl:
**some** in **any** sta za količino, ki je ne povemo natančno. Stojita z množino (**some apples**, nekaj jabolk) in z neštevnimi besedami (**some honey**, nekaj medu).

**some** je za trdilne stavke: **We've got some eggs.** (Imamo nekaj jajc.) Tudi za ponudbe in prošnje, kjer pričakujemo da: **Would you like some tea?** (Bi čaj?) **Can I have some water, please?**

**any** je za zanikane stavke in večino vprašanj: **There isn't any bread.** (Kruha ni.) **Have you got any honey?** (Imaš kaj medu?) **Are there any fish in the tarn?**

Števni samostalniki imajo množino (a sheep, fifty sheep; an apple, apples), neštevni je nimajo in ne dobijo a: honey, bread, water, milk, hay, weather, news (news je neštevni, čeprav rečemo novice). Koliko je pri števnih **how many**, pri neštevnih **how much**: **How many sheep?** **How much honey?** **a lot of** gre z obojimi: **a lot of sheep**, **a lot of honey** (veliko ovc, veliko medu). V zanikanju in vprašanjih sta pogosta tudi **many** in **much**: **We haven't got much time.** (Nimamo veliko časa.)
rule.it:
**some** e **any** indicano una quantità non precisa, come del, delle o un po' di. Vanno con il plurale (**some apples**, delle mele) e con i nomi non numerabili (**some honey**, del miele).

**some** è per le frasi affermative: **We've got some eggs.** (Abbiamo delle uova.) Anche per offrire e chiedere, quando ci si aspetta un sì: **Would you like some tea?** (Vuoi del tè?) **Can I have some water, please?**

**any** è per le frasi negative e per la maggior parte delle domande: **There isn't any bread.** (Non c'è pane.) **Have you got any honey?** (Hai del miele?) **Are there any fish in the tarn?**

I nomi numerabili hanno il plurale (a sheep, fifty sheep; an apple, apples), quelli non numerabili no e non prendono a: honey, bread, water, milk, hay, weather, news (anche se diciamo le notizie). Quanti è **how many**, quanto è **how much**: **How many sheep?** **How much honey?** **a lot of** va con tutti e due: **a lot of sheep**, **a lot of honey**. Nelle negazioni e nelle domande si usano spesso anche **many** e **much**: **We haven't got much time.** (Non abbiamo molto tempo.)
rule.de:
**some** und **any** stehen für eine Menge, die man nicht genau angibt, oft wo das Deutsche etwas, ein paar oder gar kein Wort hat. Sie stehen mit dem Plural (**some apples**, ein paar Äpfel) und mit Unzählbarem (**some honey**, etwas Honig).

**some** steht in bejahten Sätzen: **We've got some eggs.** (Wir haben Eier.) Auch in Angeboten und Bitten, wenn man ein Ja erwartet: **Would you like some tea?** **Can I have some water, please?**

**any** steht in verneinten Sätzen und den meisten Fragen: **There isn't any bread.** (Es gibt kein Brot.) **Have you got any honey?** (Hast du Honig?) **Are there any fish in the tarn?**

Zählbare Nomen haben einen Plural (a sheep, fifty sheep; an apple, apples), unzählbare nicht und bekommen kein a: honey, bread, water, milk, hay, weather, news (auch wenn es die Nachrichten heißt). Wie viele ist **how many**, wie viel ist **how much**: **How many sheep?** **How much honey?** **a lot of** geht mit beidem: **a lot of sheep**, **a lot of honey**. In Verneinung und Frage sind auch **many** und **much** üblich: **We haven't got much time.**

examples.en: Would you like some tea, Mrs Hartley?

note.en: An offer: some, even in a question.
note.it: Un'offerta: some, anche se è una domanda.
note.de: Ein Angebot: some, auch in der Frage.

examples.en: Have we got any eggs, Granny?

examples.de: Es ist keine Milch mehr da.

examples.en: Beekeeper Arthur has got a lot of honey this year.
examples.sl: Čebelar Arthur ima letos veliko medu.
examples.it: Quest'anno l'apicoltore Arthur ha tanto miele.
examples.de: Imker Arthur hat dieses Jahr viel Honig.

examples.en: How many sheep has Jack got? — A lot!
examples.de: Wie viele Schafe hat Jack? — Ganz viele!

note.en: Sheep can be counted: how many.
note.it: Le pecore si contano: how many.
note.de: Schafe kann man zählen: how many.

examples.en: How much hay do the ponies need?
examples.de: Wie viel Heu brauchen die Ponys?

note.en: Hay can't be counted: how much.
note.it: Il fieno non si conta: how much.

examples.en: Can I have some damson jam, please?
examples.sl: Lahko dobim malo slivove marmelade, prosim?
examples.it: Posso avere un po' di marmellata di susine, per favore?
examples.de: Kann ich bitte etwas Pflaumenmarmelade haben?
